text:
incident-bot: PAGING: P1 detected — Newport (vpc-newport-01) dedicated pool experiencing latency and tail error rate increase. Trigger: 95th token latency > 800ms for 3m. Affected routes: /v1/generate (nvpt-42). Paging oncall.
Ben: oncall here, seeing alerts. starting live triage. assigning to #sre-runbook
Alice: I'm joining the bridge. any customer-facing impact yet?
Ben: CS report shows intermittent timeouts for a subset of requests; estimate ~3% of traffic for Newport. Carlos pls confirm with customer if they see errors.
Carlos: Newport engineering confirms elevated error rate on their end, provided sample request IDs. They're in the middle of a load test but say it wasn't scheduled. Asking for mitigation asap.
Ben: OK. initial hypothesis: noisy tenant nvpt-42 consuming GPU memory and causing eviction/queueing. Will try tenant isolation and throttle at router layer. Alice take lead on isolation + commands.
Alice: running isolation playbook now. steps:
```
# isolate tenant nvpt-42
redwoodctl tenant isolate --tenant nvpt-42 --pool vpc-newport-01
# apply emergency throttle
redwoodctl route throttle --tenant nvpt-42 --rate 10rps
``` 
Alice: issuing commands — isolating now. watching metrics.
Ben: notifying infra to scale a temporary spare node if needed. @Frank can you spin up a hot spare in us-west-2?
Frank: starting a hot-spare GPU instance and attaching to dedicated pool. ETA ~6m. will monitor for queue drain.
Erin: adding KV cache bypass to reduce memory pressure for affected shard.
Alice: isolation succeeded. nvpt-42 traffic dropped to <0.1% of pool. latency 95th now dropped from 850ms -> 120ms within 90s. error rate trending down.
Ben: good. begin slow drain of the isolated tenant to a quarantine pool and capture logs for RCA. Carlos please draft an initial customer-facing note: what happened, what we did, ETA for full remediation.
Carlos: on it. sending preliminary note to Newport: "We've isolated a noisy process in your dedicated pool, mitigations in place, working on root cause and next steps." Will paste draft here in 10m.
Ben: quick checklist for post-live:
- capture kernel/GPU metrics for nvpt-42 (Alice)
- collect router logs and request ids (Erin)
- timeline + screenshots (Frank)
- draft incident summary and credit recommendation (Dana)
- exec briefing slice for AMs (Ben)
Dana: I'll prep credit calc and SLA impact. initial guess: 3% of requests impacted for ~8m => propose 10% credit for the billing window. will confirm.
Alice: saving all runbook actions to incident ticket #INC-639012. attaching command outputs.

--- 45 minutes later ---
Ben: closing live mitigation. metrics stable. handoff to post-incident track. moving to follow-up: RCA + exec note.
Carlos: Newport asked for an exec-level summary and timeline. want it by EOD their timezone (CEST). can we get a one-page by 4pm CEST?
Dana: I'll own the credit proposal and the customer comms with Carlos. tagging @Ben for technical review and @Frank for config notes.
Frank: I captured the GPU scheduling logs — suspicious pattern: large concurrent ephemeral streams from a single API key. saving artifacts to /artifacts/incident-639012/.
Erin: added a recommendation to add tenant-level burst limits and a routing fallback for dedicated pools.
Ben: drafting RCA outline. will include:
- what happened (noisy tenant spike, eviction)
- immediate mitigations (isolation, throttle, hot-spare)
- root cause analysis (scheduled load test from customer non-identifiable process / model warmed unexpectedly / client retry storm)
- remediation & long-term actions (tenant burst caps, improved detection, better customer guidance)

Alice: tagging runbook gaps — need a faster path to quarantine pool and an automated credit calc.
Dana: draft credit calc: 10% credit for impacted billing window, plus waived overage fees if any. will sync with finance.
Carlos: sending customer note draft now for internal review.

Carlos: "Hi Newport team — quick update: we observed a noisy workload in your dedicated pool causing elevated latency and intermittent errors. We isolated the offending tenant, applied throttles, and added a hot spare to stabilize. We're compiling a full RCA and recommended credits. ETA for detailed report: 24 hours; exec summary: 6 hours. — Carlos (Redwood CS)"
Ben: minor edits: include exact times and the ticket link. then send.

--- Next day follow-up ---
Ben: RCA draft uploaded to /incidents/639012/rca-draft.md. requesting tech approvals from Alice & Frank and exec signoff from Dana.
Alice: reviewed. added deeper GPU mem/pinning analysis and timeline adjustments.
Frank: approved. added config diff for routing change and a sample policy.
Dana: approved the credit plan. will prepare the customer SLA letter and the exec brief.
Carlos: Newport accepted the interim comms and requested the final RCA + credit agreement. they also asked for a short 30m sync with their CTO.
Ben: scheduled 30m CT with Newport CTO for 15:00 CEST. Dana and Carlos to lead customer conversation; Alice/Frank on-call for tech questions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Ticket INC-639012 moved to postmortem state.
